```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(sjPlot)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)

# 3,200 test observations exceeds the 3,000 default, which silently disables
# Satterthwaite d.f. and falls back to asymptotic (z) tests
emm_options(lmerTest.limit = 5000, pbkrtest.limit = 5000)
```

## Helper functions
```{r define model functions, include=FALSE}
my_tab_model <- function(model){
  tab_model(model,
          df.method = "satterthwaite",
          show.stat = TRUE,
          CSS = list(css.tdata = 'padding:0.1cm;padding-left:0.2cm;padding-right:0.2cm;'),
          transform = NULL,
          string.stat = "t",
          string.p = "p > |t|",
          show.re.var = FALSE,
          show.icc = FALSE,
          show.r2 = FALSE,
          wrap.labels = 100,
          show.ngroups = FALSE,
          show.obs = FALSE)
}

scale_this <- function(x){
  (x - mean(x, na.rm=TRUE)) / sd(x, na.rm=TRUE)
}

paired_report <- function(a, b, label){
  d  <- a - b
  tt <- t.test(a, b, paired = TRUE)
  sprintf("%-52s %+.4f [%+.4f, %+.4f], t(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3g, d_z = %.2f",
          label, mean(d), tt$conf.int[1], tt$conf.int[2],
          tt$parameter, tt$statistic, tt$p.value, mean(d) / sd(d))
}
```

### Loading data
```{r read data, echo=T, warning=FALSE}
# the pretraining frame has no stimType / curriculum columns, so only convert
# the factors that are actually present in each file
fac <- function(df) df %>%
  mutate(across(any_of("pretraining"), ~ factor(.x, levels = c("Simple", "XOR"))),
         across(any_of("stimType"),    ~ factor(.x, levels = c("Rule", "Exception"))),
         across(any_of("curriculum"),
                ~ factor(.x, levels = c("No Curriculum", "Simple to Complex"))),
         across(any_of("seed"), as.factor))

pretrain_data <- read_csv("../data/net_exp2_pretrain.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  fac() %>% mutate(step_z = scale_this(step))

learning_data <- read_csv("../data/net_exp2_learning.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  fac() %>% mutate(step_z = scale_this(step))

test_data <- read_csv("../data/net_exp2_test.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  fac()

train_data_ctrl <- learning_data %>% filter(curriculum == "No Curriculum")
train_data_curr <- learning_data %>% filter(curriculum == "Simple to Complex")
```

### Pretraining phase (Fig. 4B)
```{r pretrain mods}
# "networks learned both tasks, but the 1-D rule was learned faster"
pre_acc_mod <- lmer(accuracy ~ pretraining * step_z + (1 | seed),
                    data = pretrain_data,
                    contrasts = list(pretraining = "contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(pre_acc_mod)

# "1-D pretraining compressed to ~1 dimension, XOR preserved ~3"
pre_end <- pretrain_data %>% filter(step == max(step))

pre_end %>% group_by(pretraining) %>%
  summarise(accuracy = mean(accuracy), acc_sd = sd(accuracy),
            pr = mean(pr), pr_sd = sd(pr), .groups = "drop")

# NOTE: pretraining runs on noiseless inputs, and both tasks are solved to the
# same end state in EVERY network -- PR is 1.000 (SD 9e-05) after Simple and
# 3.000 (SD 1e-04) after XOR, and time to criterion is identical across networks.
# A paired test on constants is meaningless (t is infinite), so this manipulation
# check is reported descriptively: means, SDs, and the range across networks.
pre_end %>% group_by(pretraining) %>%
  summarise(across(c(accuracy, pr),
                   list(mean = mean, sd = sd, min = min, max = max)),
            .groups = "drop")

# speed: first checkpoint at which each network reaches criterion
pre_speed <- pretrain_data %>%
  filter(accuracy >= 0.95) %>%
  group_by(seed, pretraining) %>%
  summarise(step_crit = min(step), .groups = "drop")
pre_speed %>% group_by(pretraining) %>%
  summarise(median = median(step_crit), sd = sd(step_crit),
            min = min(step_crit), max = max(step_crit), .groups = "drop")
```

### Transfer learning phase (Fig. 4C)
```{r train mods}
train_ctrl_mod <- lmer(p_correct ~ pretraining * stimType * step_z + (1 | seed),
                       data = train_data_ctrl,
                       contrasts = list(pretraining = "contr.sum",
                                        stimType    = "contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(train_ctrl_mod)

train_curr_mod <- lmer(p_correct ~ pretraining * stimType * step_z + (1 | seed),
                       data = train_data_curr,
                       contrasts = list(pretraining = "contr.sum",
                                        stimType    = "contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(train_curr_mod)
```


```{r learning speed}
CRIT <- 0.60
reached <- train_data_ctrl %>%
  filter(stimType == "Exception") %>%
  group_by(seed, pretraining, step) %>%
  summarise(p = mean(p_correct), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(seed, pretraining) %>%
  summarise(hit = any(p >= CRIT), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = pretraining, values_from = hit)

table(Simple = reached$Simple, XOR = reached$XOR)
mcnemar.test(table(reached$Simple, reached$XOR), correct = FALSE)

# accuracy gap on exceptions at matched steps (no censoring)
train_data_ctrl %>%
  filter(stimType == "Exception") %>%
  group_by(pretraining, step) %>%
  summarise(p = mean(p_correct), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = pretraining, values_from = p) %>%
  mutate(gap = Simple - XOR) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

### Test model (Fig. 4D)
```{r test mod}
test_mod <- lmer(p_correct ~ curriculum * pretraining * stimType + (1 | seed),
                 data = test_data,
                 contrasts = list(curriculum  = "contr.sum",
                                  pretraining = "contr.sum",
                                  stimType    = "contr.sum"))
my_tab_model(test_mod)
```

```{r test marginals}
# WEIGHTING: with contr.sum on stimType the curriculum "main effect" is the effect
# at the UNWEIGHTED average of rule and exception -- the same coding as the human
# model, and NOT the mean over the 8 stimuli (6 rule : 2 exception). Both print.
# overall curriculum effect (averaged over pretraining and stimType). This is
# ~zero, but as a CROSSOVER, not an absence: see the by-pretraining contrast.
emm_cur <- emmeans(test_mod, ~ curriculum)
emm_cur
contrast(emm_cur, method = "revpairwise", infer = TRUE)

# the crossover: curriculum helps after Simple pretraining, hurts after XOR
emm_cur_pre <- emmeans(test_mod, ~ curriculum | pretraining)
emm_cur_pre
contrast(emm_cur_pre, method = "revpairwise", infer = TRUE)

test_data %>%
  group_by(pretraining, curriculum, stimType) %>%
  summarise(m = mean(p_correct), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stimType, values_from = m) %>%
  left_join(test_data %>% group_by(pretraining, curriculum) %>%
              summarise(raw_8stim = mean(p_correct), .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("pretraining", "curriculum")) %>%
  mutate(equal_weight = (Rule + Exception) / 2)
```

```{r test contrasts}
# does pretraining still hurt exceptions under no curriculum?
# "pairwise" (not revpairwise) so the printed contrast is Simple - XOR, matching
# the direction the text describes; emmeans gives no d_z, so quote the paired
# version below for that.
contrast(emmeans(test_mod, ~ pretraining | curriculum * stimType),
         method = "pairwise", infer = TRUE)

# THE KEY RESULT: is the curriculum benefit larger after Simple pretraining?
# (the curriculum x pretraining simple effect within exception stimuli)
emm_key <- emmeans(test_mod, ~ curriculum | pretraining * stimType)
ben <- contrast(emm_key, method = "revpairwise", infer = TRUE)   # curriculum benefit
ben
contrast(ben, method = "revpairwise", by = "stimType", infer = TRUE)  # benefit difference
```

```{r test contrasts paired}
cellm <- test_data %>%
  group_by(seed, pretraining, curriculum, stimType) %>%
  summarise(p = mean(p_correct), .groups = "drop")

get <- function(pre, cur, st) cellm %>%
  filter(pretraining == pre, curriculum == cur, stimType == st) %>%
  arrange(seed) %>% pull(p)

for (st in c("Exception", "Rule")) {
  cat(paired_report(get("Simple", "Simple to Complex", st),
                    get("Simple", "No Curriculum", st),
                    paste0(st, ": curriculum benefit | Simple pretraining")), "\n")
  cat(paired_report(get("XOR", "Simple to Complex", st),
                    get("XOR", "No Curriculum", st),
                    paste0(st, ": curriculum benefit | XOR pretraining")), "\n")
}

# difference of the two benefits == the curriculum x pretraining interaction
ben_simple <- get("Simple", "Simple to Complex", "Exception") -
              get("Simple", "No Curriculum", "Exception")
ben_xor    <- get("XOR", "Simple to Complex", "Exception") -
              get("XOR", "No Curriculum", "Exception")
cat(paired_report(ben_simple, ben_xor,
                  "Exception: benefit(Simple) - benefit(XOR)"), "\n")

# pretraining effect on exceptions under no curriculum
cat(paired_report(get("Simple", "No Curriculum", "Exception"),
                  get("XOR", "No Curriculum", "Exception"),
                  "Exception, no curriculum: Simple - XOR"), "\n")
```
